_comment: Forty study questions against Trace's own lectures, written 2026-09-19.
tags[0] is the stage the question SHOULD be answered at: 'summaries' when
the course notes carry enough, 'course' when answering well needs the
instructor's actual words. That label is a judgment about this question
against this material; it is NOT a claim about how often real students
escalate. The real escalation rate is measured in production, by the
assist_sessions table, and this eval cannot stand in for it.
expect_escalation: true, false, or 'either' when both routes are
defensible and only the answer is graded.
A case with 'followups' is run as one real multi-turn session, which is
also how the cache is exercised: turn two should read what turn one wrote.

cases.question: What's the difference between a plant-wide overhead rate and departmental rates, and why would a company bother with departmental ones?
How do I compute equivalent units of production? She said the definition is on the exam so I want it exactly right.
followups: Why are materials and conversion calculated separately?
Work it for me: 8,000 units in ending WIP, 100% complete for materials and 40% for conversion, 34,500 transferred out.

cases.question: If a job has an 80% markup do I multiply the cost by 0.8 or by 1.8? I keep getting this one wrong.
Underapplied vs overapplied overhead: which is which, and which way does cost of goods sold move in each case?
What are the four job order costing documents I need to know for the quiz, and what does each one do?
Why does process costing lump labor and overhead together as conversion costs instead of keeping them separate?
Explain the contribution margin ratio and how it relates to the variable expense ratio.
Do I need to know how to actually calculate FIFO for process costing?
Give me the schedule of cost of goods manufactured formulas in order. She said they're essential for the quiz.
There are two ways to close out the overhead account at period end. What are they and when would you use each?
Explain Schumpeter's cycle of creative destruction and why the patent system is part of it.
followups: Why did he bring up the Soviet Union in the middle of that?

cases.question: What is a brain drain and which ones did we cover in class?
What's the difference between the industrial, information and molecular economies, and which kind of labor does each one replace?
He keeps saying innovation is outrunning our ability to adapt. What's the actual argument there?
What's the distinction he drew between what Orwell feared and what Huxley feared?
Define technological spillover and give me the example he used.
What's a me-too business and why is a coffee shop the example he keeps coming back to?
What were the Rainhill Trials and which locomotives entered?
What is the innovator's dilemma? Use the Blockbuster case to explain it.
Explain the four innovation stream quadrants with an example of each. I need this for the group presentation.
Exploitation versus exploration: what's the difference, and does exploitation count as innovation at all?
Explicit versus tacit knowledge. She said this is likely to matter for the exam, so why is tacit the more valuable one?
What are the five types of power we covered, with an example of each?
How does she distinguish leadership from management? She had a line about trains.
The "what business are you really in" point: which companies did she use and what's the lesson?
What are the four styles in Hershey and Blanchard's situational leadership and when do you use each?
What are the five theories of inspiration and which one did most of the class land on?
followups: Why does he say the theory you pick actually matters?

cases.question: Why does he keep insisting we need Greek? Explain the John 21 example.
Both my entrepreneurship classes use the word innovation constantly but they seem to mean different things. How is ENTR-3306 using it versus ENTR-4306?
What do I have due across all my classes in the next week?
Across all four classes, what has an instructor actually said would be on an exam?
Quiz me on process costing.
Explain activity-based costing the way she taught it in chapter 7.
What's my current grade in ACCT-4321?
Did she cover standard costing and variance analysis yet?
In the Brunel Company walkthrough my notes say a couple of different overhead numbers came up. What did she actually work in class, and which one is right?
Walk me through the Flowpack problem exactly the way she did it in class, including anything she said about where people go wrong.
He told a story about the guy who invented the intermittent windshield wiper. Tell it the way he told it, with everything he said around it.
She told an AT&T story about ringing a bell for sales. I want the whole thing, the details and the point she drew from it.
Give me back what he said about epiripto in 1 Peter 5:7, as close to how he said it as you can get.
Make me a study guide for accounting.
Study guide for ENTR-3306 please.
